section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: LineEditor replaces the standard RISC OS line-input editor with an editor which supports command history, cursor movement, insertion and overtyping, word and region operations, filename and command completion, and configurable key bindings. Programs which use gain these facilities without needing a LineEditor-specific interface.

The module maintains either one global history or a separate history for each TaskWindow. It also provides SWIs with which applications can create and manage private histories or invoke the editor directly. LineEditor is responsible for editing and history management; the calling program remains responsible for providing the input buffer, interpreting the completed line, and displaying any subsequent output.

subsection.title: Operation
subsection.p: On initialisation, LineEditor claims ReadLineV. It therefore intercepts normal calls and associates each call with the active TaskWindow. With local histories enabled, each TaskWindow receives its own history buffer. Otherwise, all callers share the global history.

History storage is allocated in the LineEditor Buffers dynamic area when dynamic areas are available, with a maximum size of 1 Mbyte. On systems without dynamic areas the module uses the RMA. The configured buffer size applies to each newly created history buffer. Changing the configured size does not resize buffers which already exist.
When a TaskWindow closes, its local editing state and local history are released. The module cannot be killed while a line is being edited or while a client-owned history buffer exists.

subsection.title: Editing facilities
subsection.p: The default key map provides character and word movement, insertion and overtyping, deletion, a mark and cut/yank operations, history traversal, history-prefix searches, filename and command completion, and function-key expansion. Use *Help LineEditor to display the current default bindings. The supplied DfltKeys and RebindKeys files describe and install alternative bindings.

History expansion recognises a leading ! followed by a history number, a negative offset, or another !, and the form ^old^new replaces text from the preceding command. A leading ~text recalls the unique history entry beginning with text. Each form can be disabled through .

subsection.title: Configuration at module start
subsection.p: The module may be started with up to five unsigned values:

p.userinput: *RMRun LineEditor size flags minimum maximum cursors

subsection.p: The values have the same meanings as R0 to R4 of . Omitted values use their defaults. The default history size is 4 Kbytes, the minimum recorded length is 1 character, there is no effective maximum recorded length, and the default cursor word is &hex;100.

subsection.title: Private history buffers
subsection.p: A client creates a private history with and passes the returned handle to the other history SWIs. Handles are opaque and remain valid until explicitly deleted, automatically deleted following the associated task's Wimp close-down, or removed when the module is reinitialised. A client must not inspect or modify a handle as an address.

Lines are numbered from zero, oldest first. The current position is independent for each private buffer. The logical position following the newest recorded line is an empty end position and can be selected with .

section.title: System Variables
section.p: These variables contain output sequences written at transitions in the editing display. They are principally intended for setting text colours in a single-tasking command-line environment. An unset variable produces no output.

sysvar-definition.name: LineEditor$Edit
sysvar-definition.description: Sequence written before editing text is displayed

use.p: The value is written before an edit begins and after a completion listing, restoring the appearance used for the prompt and editable text.
The value is written after a line edit ends, selecting the appearance used for output from the command which follows.

sysvar-definition.name: LineEditor$List
sysvar-definition.description: Sequence written while completion entries are displayed

use.p: The value is written before the completion list and again after each entry's type marker.

sysvar-definition.name: LineEditor$Type
sysvar-definition.description: Sequence written before a completion entry's type marker

use.p: The value is written between a completion name and the marker which identifies a directory, executable file, system variable, filing system or command type.
LineEditor re-establishes its workspace and ReadLineV claim following a reset. On a soft reset it first releases TaskWindow instances which are no longer valid.

service-definition.name: WimpCloseDown
service-definition.description: A Wimp task is closing down

use.p: LineEditor releases the local history and editing state belonging to the closing TaskWindow. Service calls associated with Wimp initialisation are ignored.
Displays the used, free and total byte counts and the number of recorded lines. With local histories enabled, information is shown for each history and the most recently used one is marked.
Erases the global history, or the history belonging to the most recently used TaskWindow when local histories are enabled.
Lists the recorded lines in the global history, or in the most recently used TaskWindow history when local histories are enabled. Line numbers in the display begin at 1.

command-definition.name: LoadHistory
command-definition.description: Adds lines from a text file to the current history
command-definition.parameter: Text file containing one history line per line.

use.p: Reads the file into the global history, or the most recently used local history. A history is created if none exists. Lines pass through the configured recording filters; input beyond 255 characters on one line is ignored up to the next line terminator.

command-definition.name: SaveHistory
command-definition.description: Saves the current history to a text file

use.p: Writes the global history, or the most recently used local history, in oldest-to-newest order with one entry per line. The resulting file is assigned filetype Text.
A private-history SWI was passed a handle which is not owned by LineEditor, or which has already been deleted.
An attempt was made to kill the module while a line edit was active or while a client-owned private history still existed. Finish the edit and delete every private buffer before retrying.
